title: On Predicting the storm before the glass fell
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：predict　|　正文 367 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 predict 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the postman ① predicted the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② predicts the storm before the glass fell without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ predict the storm before the glass fell at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ predicted the storm before the glass fell before — a line in the list for June 1945 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Predicting the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ predict the harvest from the blossom without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Predict the harvest from the blossom at once and never mention it again.

By 1958 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ predicts the harvest from the blossom for the whole place every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ predicted the storm before the glass fell again when nobody else would.

⑩ To predict the storm before the glass fell, my mother said in 1963, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody predicts the storm before the glass fell without a word of thanks again and somebody must predict the storm before the glass fell for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 预言（一般过去式 predicted the storm before the glass fell：1951 年邮差头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 预言（一般现在 predicts the storm before the glass fell：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 预言（不定式 to predict the storm before the glass fell：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 预言（过去完成时 had predicted the storm before the glass fell：1945 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 预言（动名词 predicting the storm before the glass fell 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 预测（predict the harvest from the blossom：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去预测从开花的样子预测这一季收成）
G. v. 预测（predict the harvest from the blossom：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 预言（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 predicts the harvest from the blossom，而母亲又一次 predicted the storm before the glass fell）

answers.why: predict 意为“预言”，1951 年邮差替所有人预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 predicted。
predict 意为“预言”，自那以后邮差不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 predicts。
predict 意为“预言”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴”，此处为不定式 to predict the storm before the glass fell。
predict 意为“预言”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1958 年之前就有人预言过，故用过去完成时 had predicted。
predict 意为“预言”，邮差说“预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 predicting the storm before the glass fell 作主语。
predict 意为“预测”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去预测从开花的样子预测这一季收成”，should ever 之后用原形 predict the harvest from the blossom。
predict 意为“预测”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻预测从开花的样子预测这一季收成（predict the harvest from the blossom at once），以后再也不要提起。
predict 意为“预言”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例预测从开花的样子预测这一季收成，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 predicts。
predict 意为“预言”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴，用一般过去式 predicted 叙述。
predict 意为“预言”，结尾那句是母亲 1963 年的话：要预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1951 年，邮差替所有人预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴；邮局里每一个寄信人都说这是头一回。（predicted the storm before the glass fell）
多年以后，邮差仍不图一句谢做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（predicts the storm before the glass fell）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴这件事本身。（to predict the storm before the glass fell）
早在 1945 年就有人预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴，六月那天收发清单上的一行字就是证据。（had predicted the storm before the glass fell）
邮差说过，替所有人预言气压计掉下来之前就说要有风暴这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（predicting the storm before the glass fell 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻预测从开花的样子预测这一季收成，以后再也不要提起。（predict the harvest from the blossom，祈使句）
answers: In 1951 the postman predicted the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three weeks on, the postman still predicts the storm before the glass fell without a word of thanks without being asked.
My mother said later that to predict the storm before the glass fell at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had predicted the storm before the glass fell long before 1958, and the line in the list for June proves it.
Predicting the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Predict the harvest from the blossom at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 predict 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1951 the postman predicted the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman predicts the storm before the glass fell without a word of thanks whenever the office asks.
Predicting the storm before the glass fell for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever predict the harvest from the blossom without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office predicts the harvest from the blossom for the whole place every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother predicted the storm before the glass fell again, and the office remembered that half.
